## Glossary

**action-rules**  
Class: the ActionRule algebra, RebacSchema actions and per-record permissionRules.

**ActionRule**  
string | { rel, action } | { rule } | { any } | { all } | boolean | null: what one action means.

**actor**  
Class: who is acting, set with permix.setActor({ model, record }) and read by rules as __actor.

**__actor**  
Reserved key holding { model, record } of who is acting; null when nobody is.

**any / all**  
OR and AND composition of ActionRules; all is how a rule narrows.

**bridge**  
A json-rules Bridge between two fieldMaps declared in schema.bridges; only to-one directions walk.

**bridges**  
Class: cross-source rel walks through schema bridges and far rows passed as subject.data.

**map:model**  
A map-qualified resource key (db:User, crm:Account) used in schemas and as bridge segments.

**{ ok, errors }**  
The json-rules result shape every validator returns.

**own-row rule**  
{ rel: 'user', action } on a row hydrated with its user; there is no self arm.

**permissionRules**  
A record's JSON field action → ActionRule, ORed with the schema rule; only widens.

**positive rule**  
No negation, isEmpty, notExists, if/then/else, array or aggregate rule; validateRule(..., { positive: true }).

**Pseudo record**  
A would-be row a create or grant is checked on before it exists.

**RebacSchema**  
{ bridges?, permissions: { [resource]: { actions: { [name]: ActionRule } } } }.

**{ rel, action }**  
Walk a dotted to-one relation path (space.organization) and check action on the target.

**{ rule }**  
A positive json-rules Condition over the record, with the actor under __actor.

**rule-validation**  
Class: keeping rules positive and acyclic with validateActionRule, validateSchema and schemaRuleIssues.

**schemaRuleIssues**  
Lists every schema rule that is not well formed and positive, without the map or cycle check.

**string delegation**  
An ActionRule that is another action's name on the same resource (manage: 'own').

**subject.data**  
Far rows backing bridge hops, keyed map:model; a missing far row denies.

**terminal null**  
Denies by rule; the top of a chain (own: null) is reached only by grants or row rules.

**validateActionRule**  
Checks one serialized ActionRule's shape and positivity; with { schema, resource, action } also refuses cycles.

**validateSchema**  
Checks a whole schema against a SchemaMap: rules, rel segments, defined actions; for a test or boot.

## 1. What this Warden covers

How an app says what each of its actions means on each resource: the positive ActionRule algebra in a RebacSchema, per-record permissionRules that only widen, rules over the actor under __actor, bridges to other data sources, and the validators that keep rules positive and acyclic.

## 2. The domain

A RebacSchema maps each resource to its actions, and each action to an ActionRule. A string delegates to another action on the same resource (a chain like own ⊇ manage ⊇ read, with null at the top so only grants reach it). { rel, action } walks a dotted to-one relation path and checks the action there. { rule } is a json-rules condition over the record, and the actor sits under __actor. any and all compose rules. null, false and an action the schema doesn't name all deny. Action names are the app's own. A record's permissionRules field adds a rule per action, ORed with the schema rule, so it can widen access and never revoke it. There is no self arm and no actor arm: acting on your own row is { rel: 'user', action } on a row hydrated with its user, and a condition about who is acting is a plain { rule } on __actor.model or __actor.record.

Rules are positive only. Narrow access with all, never with a deny. validateActionRule checks one stored rule (a tenant-authored or row rule) before you persist it, and with a context it also refuses a cycle back to its own action. validateSchema checks a whole schema against the SchemaMap in a test or at boot: rules, rel segments and named actions. schemaRuleIssues lists only the malformed or non-positive rules, which is the test a check runs before it throws. Bridges let a rel segment named map:model cross to another source. The far rows come in as subject.data, and an absent far row denies.

Running the check, the SchemaMap and hydration belong to running-a-check. Grants, entitlements and who may grant them belong to grants-and-entitlements. Not here: calling check or createRebacPaths and loading records (running-a-check); the permix, entitlements, granting and delegates (grants-and-entitlements); comparisons with other systems and the unbuilt reflection to queries (library-scope).

<!-- unit doc:README.md#permission-algebra-actionrule -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Permission algebra (`ActionRule`) (in "@inixiative/permissions")

#### Permission algebra (`ActionRule`)

```ts
type ActionRule =
  | string                       // rbac: delegate to another action on the same resource
  | { rel: string; action: string }  // rebac: walk a relation, then check `action` on the target
  | { rule: Condition }          // abac: a json-rules predicate over the record, the actor under `__actor`
  | { any: ActionRule[] }        // OR
  | { all: ActionRule[] }        // AND
  | boolean                      // terminal: `true` allows, `false` denies
  | null;                        // terminal deny, as is an action the schema does not name
```

A `RebacSchema` is `{ bridges?, permissions }`. `permissions` maps a (map-qualified) **resource**,
e.g. `db:User`, to `{ actions: { name → ActionRule } }`; `bridges` are the cross-source edges a `rel`
walk may cross (see [Bridges](#bridges-cross-source-rel-walks)). A single-source schema omits
`bridges` and can use bare resource keys.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#writing-a-schema -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Writing a schema (in "@inixiative/permissions")

#### Writing a schema

Action names are **yours**: the engine imposes no vocabulary. The `own`/`manage`/`read` chain below
is illustrative; use whatever your roles grant.

```ts
import { Operator } from '@inixiative/json-rules';
import type { RebacSchema } from '@inixiative/permissions';

const schema: RebacSchema = {
  permissions: {
    organization: {
      actions: {
        own: null, //         terminal: granted only via permix (roles) or row rules
        manage: 'own', //     delegation chain — own ⊇ manage ⊇ read
        read: 'manage',
      },
    },
    membership: {
      actions: {
        read: { any: [{ rel: 'user', action: 'read' }, { rel: 'organization', action: 'read' }] },
        leave: { rel: 'user', action: 'operate' }, // your own row: a walk to your own user entry
        manage: { rel: 'organization', action: 'manage' },
      },
    },
    document: {
      actions: {
        read: {
          any: [
            { rule: { field: 'isPublic', operator: Operator.equals, value: true } }, // abac guard
            { rel: 'organization', action: 'read' }, // rebac: walk the relation
          ],
        },
        manage: { rel: 'organization', action: 'manage' },
      },
    },
  },
};
```

`rel` accepts dot-paths for multi-hop walks: `{ rel: 'space.organization', action: 'own' }` chains
through `record.space.organization`, resolving each hop's model from the schema map.

Records may also carry a `permissionRules` JSON field (`action → ActionRule`): a per-record rule (a
condition, a relation walk or both), so one record can take a rule its model's schema doesn't. `check` merges a row
rule **additively** (OR) with the schema rule, so per-record overrides can widen but never revoke.
`check` validates a row rule before merging it: one that isn't positive, or that delegates back to
its own action (a cycle), widens nothing. Validate tenant-authored rules with `validateActionRule`
before persisting them too, so the author hears about it.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#also-exported -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Also exported (in "@inixiative/permissions")

#### Also exported

- `validateActionRule(rule, context?)` checks a serialized `ActionRule` (tenant/row overrides)
  the way json-rules `validateRule` checks a condition, and returns the same `{ ok, errors }`: the
  shape, and every `{ rule }` a positive json-rules condition. Given `{ schema, resource, action,
  rowRules? }`, it also refuses a rule that delegates back to its own action through the schema or
  the record's other rules. No schema library involved.
- `validateSchema(map, schema)` checks a whole schema against the map, for a test or boot: every
  rule as `validateActionRule` checks it (cycles included), every `{ rel }` segment a relation or a
  bridge, and every action a rule names defined where it lands. Same `{ ok, errors }`, each issue's
  `path` starting `resource.action`.
- `schemaRuleIssues(schema)` returns the issues of every schema rule that is not well formed and
  positive, without the map or the cycle check. It is the test a check runs on a schema's first use
  before it throws.
- `PermissionsEngineGlobals` types the engine setting this package registers,
  `permissions.idField` (see [The check engine](#the-check-engine)), so
  `engineGlobals.set('permissions.idField', 'uuid')` typechecks without redeclaring it.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#the-actor -->
**Source:** `README.md` § The actor (in "@inixiative/permissions")

#### The actor

The actor is who is acting: what kind of credential (`model`) and its row (`record`). The app sets
it once per request; a `{ rule }` reads it under the reserved key `__actor`, like any other data:

```ts
permix.setActor({ model: 'User', record: user });   // a person, acting directly
permix.setActor({ model: 'Token', record: token }); // a token, with whatever owner relations you loaded

// person-only
{ rule: { field: '__actor.model', operator: Operator.equals, value: 'User' } }
// the record against the actor's row
{ rule: { field: 'ownerId', operator: Operator.equals, path: '__actor.record.userId' } }
```

It is just a rule. With nobody acting, `__actor` is null and the rule runs as written; a rule that
needs someone acting names who (`__actor.model equals 'User'` inside its `all`), since rules are
positive. Beware a comparison against a field that may be null: with
nobody acting, `ownerId equals __actor.record.id` holds when `ownerId` is null. A row's `permissionRules` read it the same way and still only widen. A superadmin skips
the schema, so it skips these too.

<!-- unit doc:README.md#bridges-cross-source-rel-walks -->
**Source:** `README.md` § Bridges (cross-source `rel` walks) (in "@inixiative/permissions")

#### Bridges (cross-source `rel` walks)

A `rel` can cross a **bridge**: a cross-source edge between two fieldMaps (see
[`@inixiative/json-rules`](https://github.com/inixiative/json-rules)). Declare them on the schema;
both ends are map-qualified resources:

```ts
const schema: RebacSchema = {
  bridges: [{
    endpoints: [
      { fieldMap: 'crm', model: 'Account', on: 'id' },
      { fieldMap: 'db',  model: 'User',    on: 'accountId' },
    ],
    cardinality: 'oneToMany',
  }],
  permissions: {
    'db:User':     { actions: { read: { rel: 'crm:Account', action: 'own' } } },
    'crm:Account': { actions: { own: null } },
  },
};
```

Bridges **don't hydrate** (they aren't FK relations). The join key is a scalar on the record
(`User.accountId`); pass the far rows as `subject.data` (keyed `map:model`, the `indexBridges`
shape) and the engine builds the lookup itself. A far row absent from `subject.data` denies the
walk, whatever the far action is, an rbac grant on the far id included:

```ts
check(permix, schema, {
  resource: 'db:User',
  record: { id: 'u1', accountId: 'acc1' },
  data: { 'crm:Account': [{ id: 'acc1', tier: 'gold' }] },
}, 'read');
```
